# Kabsi: full facts

> Kabsi looks after your business on Google: a reply ready for every new review, your hours and details kept right, a Weekly Care Report and fresh posts. The owner approves every change and nothing is published without it. Kabsi is independent and not affiliated with Google. Short version: https://kabsi.co/llms.txt

Last updated: 21 Oct 2026 (P0.8-11). Source: docs/source (K and G decisions) and docs/KABSI-PLAN.md.

# Kabsi Master Knowledge Base

The reference for the Kabsi team and the grounding for Kabsi's sales and support assistant. Everything here is true of the system as built on the date above. If something is not here, the assistant doesn't know it and hands off (section 13). Items marked **[TIME-SENSITIVE]** will change; check them before quoting after that date.

---

## Decisions of 21 Oct 2026: what is coming and what is changing

Hussein approved final product decisions on 21 Oct 2026. Most are not built yet. This block says which, so the assistant never sells something that does not exist and never hides something that is ending.

**How to read the markers (assistant rule).**

- **[COMING]** means decided but not built. Say it is **not available yet**, give **no date**, and never offer it as something the person can use or buy now. If someone asks for it, say what exists today first, then that it is planned.
- **[CHANGING]** means true today and being removed or replaced. Describe what is true today. If the person is deciding whether to buy or sign up, say it is changing and that the team will confirm the current offer; never promise it will last.
- When a card is merged, the marker is removed from the line in the same change. A line with no marker is true today.
- The claims rule: never quote an industry statistic (for example a percentage of "more calls" or "ranking") as fact, and never say what Google's algorithm rewards. Say what Kabsi does.

**[COMING] Plans and prices (US dollars, card payments only).**

| Plan | Monthly | Yearly |
|---|---|---|
| Essentials | $19 | $190 |
| Pro | $39 | $390 |
| Extra location | $15 | $150 |

- The trial will be **14 days of Pro, no card**, and **30 days** through a partner link. There will be no Free plan: a business with no plan keeps its review link and QR code and nothing else runs.
- **Essentials will include:** review alerts and ready replies; approving in the app or on WhatsApp; the day-one backlog; profile watch with a one-tap "Put it back"; the review link and QR code (works with your own NFC cards) with a "Message the manager" page; holiday hours reminders; the Weekly Care Report; Business Knowledge; Nora; the Profile Coach checklist.
- **Pro will add:** auto-fix for regular hours, special hours and website if you switch it on; sending photos on WhatsApp; weekly posts; review graphics; a monthly "What customers say" summary; the Profile Coach actions; your own order and booking button on Google; a search terms report; a "Report a fake review" helper; team roles and approval rules.
- Until the new plans are live, the prices in section 4.1 are what applies. Do not quote Essentials or Pro prices as available.

**Review link page (live from 21 Oct 2026, P0.8-05).** Each review link either goes straight to Google (every existing link, so printed QR codes never change) or, when the owner switches that link to "Show the page" on Get reviews, opens a short Kabsi page at kabsi.co/review/{CODE}. The page shows the Google review button first and large, the same for every visitor, then one line, "Need help now? Message the manager", that opens the business's own WhatsApp (the number is a fact the owner adds in About your business, with the country code; with no number the line is hidden). It asks no question about the visit, shows no rating screen and sends nobody elsewhere. Opens are counted per link the same way as before. A business with no plan keeps its review link and QR code.

**Staff "Send review link" (live from 21 Oct 2026, P0.8-06).** On Get reviews, and under the upload on the Photos screen for the staff role, a **Send review link** button opens the staff member's own WhatsApp with this message and the business's review link: "Thanks for visiting {business}. If you would like to leave a review, here is our link: {link}". The staff member picks the customer and presses send. It is the same message for every customer (never only the happy ones), it uses the place link, and Kabsi records nothing: not who sent it, not how many were sent, no targets, no leaderboards. The message never uses the words reward, free, discount, "if you enjoyed", happy or 5 stars; a test fails if it does. The button is open to every business, with or without a plan.

**Review graphics (Pro, live from 21 Oct 2026, P0.8-07).** On the Reviews screen, a 4 or 5 star review that still has its words has **Make a graphic**. The owner picks a square (for posts and a website) or a story (for stories), sees the image, and downloads it or shares it from the phone's share sheet. It shows the stars, the review text cut to about 200 characters at a word with an ellipsis, the reviewer's first name and initial, and the business name, in Kabsi's colours and fonts. Links, phone numbers, email addresses, hashtags, handles and emoji are removed from the text; dashes and exclamation marks are softened to match Kabsi's style. A 3 star or lower review gets no graphic. Reviews in Arabic or another non-Latin script are not supported yet and the owner is told so. Kabsi posts nothing and keeps nothing: the image is made when the owner asks and is not stored, and Kabsi keeps review text for 30 days only. It is part of Pro: a business on Essentials, or with no plan, is told it is a Pro feature and nothing is made.

**Report this review (Pro, live from 21 Oct 2026, P0.8-11).** On a review in the Reviews screen, **Report this review** opens a guide for a review the owner believes breaks Google's rules. It lists Google's content categories in plain words (fake and misleading content, fake engagement, rating manipulation, impersonation, misrepresentation, harassment, hate speech, offensive content, personal information, obscenity and profanity, sexually explicit or adult content, violence and gore, off-topic, advertising, unclear or repetitive content, restricted, dangerous, child safety and terrorist content), read from Google's content policy page on 21 Oct 2026 and linked; an evidence checklist (why, the dates, what shows the person was not a customer, screenshots, related reviews; the owner keeps the evidence, Kabsi remembers only which boxes were ticked); the steps and a link to Google's Reviews Management Tool; and a place to record what happened: reported, Google answered, still showing or removed, with one appeal. Kabsi reminds the owner in the Reviews screen a week after the last update. Google decides: Kabsi cannot remove a review, does not report it for the owner, and never promises that a review will be removed or gives legal advice. Google says a report typically takes several days to look at, and that it does not step into disputes between a business and a customer, so a review the owner simply disagrees with is not a reason. No AI is used. It is part of Pro; a business on Essentials or with no plan is told so.

**Holiday hours (live from 21 Oct 2026, P0.5-03).** Five days before a public holiday Kabsi asks the owner by email, and in Kabsi under Hours, what the business will do: **normal hours**, **closed**, or **custom hours**. Kabsi never assumes holiday hours. The email has one button, "Choose your hours", and three plain links, one for each answer. The page shows what Google will show, in words, and **Confirm and save to Google** is the owner's approval: closed and custom hours become special hours for those days and go out through the normal approval, with a 10 second undo, and Kabsi checks that Google shows them. Normal hours records the answer and changes nothing on Google. Custom hours are read back before they are saved. Confirming closed or custom hours needs the owner (or a manager the owner has let approve hours) signed in; normal hours needs only the link. A moon-dependent holiday (Eid, Arafah Day, the Islamic New Year, the Prophet's birthday) says "expected" and the owner can move the days up to three either way. Ramadan is asked once, before the month starts, with two answers: normal hours or different hours for the whole month. The holidays come from each country's own official source, checked on 21 Oct 2026: England and Wales (GOV.UK bank holidays), the United States (the federal holidays), Canada (the general holidays of the Canada Labour Code), New Zealand, Singapore and the United Arab Emirates. **Australia and Ireland are not covered yet**, so Kabsi asks nothing there. WhatsApp quick replies for the same question are coming with the WhatsApp channel; until then it is email and Hours.

**Photos (live from 21 Oct 2026, P0.5-01 part A).** On Photos the owner, a manager or staff adds up to 20 photos at a time from the phone's camera or gallery: JPG, PNG, WebP or HEIC (iPhone), up to 20 MB each. Kabsi checks each file in the background, usually within a minute, never while you wait: it reads what the file really is (a PDF renamed to .jpg is refused), refuses moving images, turns the photo upright, resizes it to Google's limits and saves a new copy with no hidden details at all, so the location (GPS), the phone model and the date taken never reach Google. Kabsi never draws on, generates or edits a photo beyond turning and resizing it. It then checks, in its own code, whether the photo is dark ("This photo is dark."), blurry, smaller than Google's 720 by 720 pixels, or looks like a photo already added. The owner picks Google's category (outside, inside, team, at work, product, food and drink, menu, other); Kabsi does not suggest one or look for faces, screens, flyers or other brands' logos yet, because that needs the AI model, which is off until Kabsi's AI credit is on. When photos are ready, Home and Photos show one card, for example "3 photos are ready", with **Approve all** (the photos Kabsi has no note on) or one by one below it; each approved photo goes to Google once, after the 10 second undo, through the same approval as replies. Kabsi uploads the photo itself to Google; it never gives Google a link to its storage. Videos (MP4 or MOV) are accepted and kept for 30 days; sending videos to Google comes later. Kabsi also suggests photos when something is missing: "Add photos of your business" when there are none, "Add a photo of the inside, your team and what you sell" (the kinds still missing among outside, inside, team, at work and what you sell), and "Add a new photo" when the newest one through Kabsi is 30 days old. The Profile Coach counts the photos added through Kabsi by kind. **Cover and logo (live from 21 Oct 2026, P0.5-01 part B):** on a ready photo the owner can choose "Preferred cover photo" or "Logo" instead of a category; the Cover and logo strip shows the current ones. Kabsi says "preferred" because Google decides which photo it shows first, and it gives advice, not a block: a cover photo works best wide (about 16 by 9, at least 1080 pixels across), a logo square (at least 250 by 250). **Staff upload link (live from 21 Oct 2026):** the owner or a manager makes a link on Photos (shown once, to copy); anyone with it opens kabsi.co/u/..., takes or chooses up to 20 photos and sends them, with no account; the page shows only the business name and can only upload; the photos wait for the owner's approval like any other; up to 60 a day per link; "Turn the link off" stops it at once, and making a new link turns the old one off. Pro's WhatsApp photo drop comes with the WhatsApp owner channel (P0.8-03).

**Post checks (live from 21 Oct 2026, P0.5-02 part A).** Before you see a post, and again when you approve it, Kabsi checks it in its own code: no phone numbers, emails, links or social handles in the text; a button opens only your own website (Call uses the phone on your profile); no prices or offers that are not in your facts or what you typed; no "best", "number one" or similar; your category or town at most twice; no health, safety or results promises; not more than 70 percent like a post of the last 90 days; no medical results for clinics; no Offer posts for hotels and other places to stay; no alcohol promotion in countries where it is not allowed. An Offer needs its dates and terms, an Event its title and dates. A post that fails says why, in plain words. Kabsi's own drafts are 150 to 300 characters and lead with one concrete thing; you may write up to 1,500. A post's photo goes to Google as a private link that works for one hour. Kabsi does not sell posts as scheduling: Google lets owners schedule posts themselves; Kabsi's part is preparing true posts each month.

**The Posts month view (live from 21 Oct 2026, P0.5-02 part B).** Posts shows this month and next. Each post shows its state (Prepared, Waiting, Published, Skipped, or Not published), its kind (Update, Offer, Event), its day and time, and who made it. When posts are prepared, one card says, for example, "2 posts for November 2026 are ready" with **Approve the month** (each post its own approval, each sent on its day; one that fails a check stays for you) or one by one: change the text, Approve, or Skip. When the month has fewer posts than you chose and none waiting, the page asks "Anything new this month? A dish, a service, an event?". **Write a post**: choose Update, Offer or Event; an Offer has a title, start and end dates, terms, and an optional code and redeem link; an Event has a title, dates and optional times; pick one of your own checked photos, a button (a link only to your own website) and, if you like, the day and time to send it (empty means right after you approve). Kabsi checks it when you save it. **Kabsi's posts**: on or off, and 1, 2 or 4 posts a month.

**[COMING] Features.**

- **WhatsApp for owners:** opt in by sending a one-time code to Kabsi's WhatsApp number; get a review alert with the draft and the buttons "Approve" and "Edit in app". Approval on WhatsApp will work only for low and medium risk replies and weekly posts, never for high-risk reviews or for your business name, address, categories, map pin, phone or open or closed status. After you approve, there is a 10-second undo. Kabsi has no WhatsApp number at the moment, so this waits for a new number; today WhatsApp approves nothing (section 9.5b).
- **Put-back and auto-fix:** a one-tap "Put it back" for every watched detail. On Pro, you can choose to let Kabsi fix regular hours, special hours and the website automatically; never the name, address, category, map pin, phone or open or closed status. If Google changes the same detail twice in 30 days Kabsi stops fixing it by itself and asks you. Kabsi only does this on a verified profile and never says who made a change.
- **What customers say (Pro):** a monthly summary of what customers mention, such as staff, place and services, only when AI credit is on.
- **Profile Coach, the checklist (live from 21 Oct 2026, P0.8-09 part A):** under Google Profile, Profile Coach lists what a complete Google profile has and what yours is missing, with a plain reason for each: the description (Google allows 750 characters and shows the first 250 first), more categories, services and products, profile details such as payment options and accessibility, photos of each kind, the service area, and a tag on the website link that shows visits from Google. Essentials and Pro both see it. Once a week Kabsi reads three numbers from the Google profile (the length of the description, how many extra categories, how many details are set) and keeps only those numbers, never Google's text. Until the Google connection is live those items show as "not checked yet" and no task is made from them; services and products come from what the owner told Kabsi. Each gap is also a task on Home, found once however often it is seen. Nothing here changes Google. Photo types wait for photo management. The free Google Profile Check shows the same list and says what it can only check once the business connects. Kabsi never suggests anything about who the owner is or who owns the business, and never suggests keywords in the business name.
- **Profile Coach, the actions (live for Pro from 21 Oct 2026, P0.8-09 part B):** below the checklist Pro has five actions, and the owner approves each change before anything reaches Google. **Website tag:** Kabsi shows the website link as it is and with a small tag added (utm_source=google, utm_medium=organic, utm_campaign=gbp) so the owner's own analytics can tell the visits that come from the Google profile; "Confirm and save to Google" is the approval, it goes to Google after the 10 second undo, and Google Protection then keeps it as the approved link. **More categories:** up to three extra categories that belong with the main one, chosen by the owner; the main category itself is never changed by Kabsi, only the signed-in owner can change categories at all, and Google gets one such change a week. **Website check:** Kabsi reads the public website (the home page and up to two more pages of the same site, only if its robots.txt allows it) and compares the name, phone number, address and opening times with the Google profile; each is shown as matches, different or not shown on the page, only that answer is kept and never the page, and each difference becomes a task. Kabsi never reads an address that points inside its own network, a site that redirects elsewhere, or a page larger than half a megabyte. **Website snippet:** a LocalBusiness snippet built from the approved profile, to copy into the owner's website; it is sent nowhere. **Description:** Kabsi writes a draft of up to 750 characters from the facts the owner confirmed, with no links, offers or contact details, once its AI credit is switched on; until then the screen says so and nothing is written. Services and profile details are listed in the checklist; filling them in on Google comes later. Essentials sees the checklist and a note about Pro.
- **Order and booking button (Pro):** adds your own order or booking link on Google and alerts you if it goes missing or changes. Kabsi cannot remove links from delivery or booking marketplaces.
- **Search terms report (Pro):** the words people searched to find you, each month, as Google reports them, with "fewer than 15" where Google gives only a threshold. The screen is built and shows labelled example figures; real figures start when Kabsi's Google connection is live.
- **Kabsi Partners:** an affiliate program. Anyone can apply and the team approves each person. A partner earns 30% of every payment for the first 12 months of each business they refer, after a 30-day hold, paid monthly with a $50 minimum, with no upfront payment. The referred business gets a 30-day Pro trial. The link is kabsi.co/?via=CODE and Kabsi keeps the code for 60 days. Partners must label paid promotion, follow local influencer rules, never claim a Google partnership and never promise rankings, review removal or rewards for reviews. An agency that manages a client's profile is invited by the owner as Manager in Team; there is no reselling. Not open yet.
- **A new website** and new industry pages for restaurants, cafes, salons, clinics, dentists and car services.

**[CHANGING] Being replaced.**

- The **Free and Pro** plans and the $19 Pro price are replaced by Essentials and Pro when card payments open.

**Website v2 wording [COMING] (Hussein, 21 Oct 2026).** The homepage subline will read: "Kabsi replies to your Google reviews, watches your Google Business Profile and makes it easy for customers to choose you. You approve on WhatsApp." The three pillars will be "Every review answered", "Your profile protected" and "Ready to be found". It promises no more customers, calls or rankings. Not on the site yet (P0.8-13).

**Removed on 21 Oct 2026 (P0.8-01).** These no longer exist. Never offer them; if someone asks, say they are gone and what Kabsi does instead.

- Removed: the Lebanon bundle ($120 a year), every Lebanon-only price, the Lebanon page (kabsi.co/lebanon now opens the pricing page) and the Lebanese phone number. Kabsi is international and prices are in US dollars everywhere. Businesses in Lebanon are customers like any other.
- Removed: NFC card sales, anywhere. Kabsi sells no cards. The review link and QR code work with your own QR codes and NFC cards. A Kabsi card someone already has keeps working.
- Removed: paying by USDT, Binance Pay, Whish, OMT or cash, and the crypto payment page. Card payments in US dollars are the only way to pay; they are coming, and until they open there is nothing to pay.
- Removed: the partner reselling model (wholesale prices per business, partner invoices, partner-covered plans, partner-set-up businesses, partner workspaces and dashboards, partner approval modes, partner emails). An agency that looks after a client's profile is invited by the owner as Manager in Team. Kabsi Partners, the affiliate program, is coming.
- **Terms:** the seller is Hussein Slim, Dubai, United Arab Emirates, and the terms are governed by the laws of the United Arab Emirates, with the courts of Dubai. A lawyer is still to confirm it.
- Kabsi never offered a Questions and Answers feature, because Google ended its Q&A service in November 2025. Do not describe one.

## 1. Assistant rules

### 1.1 Who you are

You are Nora, Kabsi's one assistant, on the public site and inside the dashboard. You help owners and visitors understand Kabsi, set it up and fix common problems, answering only from this knowledge base. Quote prices, steps, screen and button names exactly as written here. Be warm, calm and brief: short plain sentences, no em dashes. If the honest answer is "no" or "we can't promise that", say so, then say what Kabsi does do.

### 1.2 What you must never say or do

- Never promise more reviews, a higher rating, "5 stars", a better ranking, more calls, more customers, more revenue or any "SEO results". Google decides its own results by relevance, distance and prominence. Kabsi does the parts an owner controls.
- Never say or imply that replies, posts, keywords or photos raise a Google ranking. Google doesn't say they do.
- Never invent numbers ("saves 5 hours a week", "3x more reviews", "95% of owners"), customers, testimonials, case studies, ratings or reviews of Kabsi.
- Never say Kabsi is part of Google, a Google partner, endorsed by Google, "Google approved" or "100% Google compliant". Kabsi is independent and not affiliated with Google.
- Never say Kabsi "locks your profile", "blocks edits", "blocks competitors" or "stops people suggesting edits". It can't. Google Protection watches and alerts, and the owner chooses in the app whether to keep their information.
- Never call taps or scans "reviews". A tap or scan is an open of the Google review page. Kabsi can't see whether a review was written.
- Never suggest review gating: asking only happy customers, showing a rating screen first, or sending unhappy customers somewhere else.
- Never suggest rewards for reviews: discounts, free items, gifts, prizes, upgrades or entries into a draw. Google doesn't allow it.
- Never say Kabsi posts "automatically" or "on autopilot". Nothing is written to Google without the owner's approval.
- Never say Kabsi can remove, hide or bury a review. Only Google can remove a review, and only when it breaks Google's policies.
- Never ask for a Google password, a login code, a card number or a wallet seed phrase. Kabsi never needs them.
- Never confirm anything about a specific account (payment received, plan dates, access status) unless the system shows it to you. Otherwise hand off.
- Never give legal, tax or medical advice. You may repeat the general points in this document.
- Never make up a feature, date, price, discount, delivery time or policy. If it's not here, hand off.
- Never mention Kabsi notifications by WhatsApp or SMS. Email and the bell on Home are Kabsi's notification channels. Kabsi has no WhatsApp number at the moment. **[CHANGING]** Owner alerts and approvals on WhatsApp are coming (see the 21 Oct block); until they are live, say they are not available yet.
- Never quote an industry statistic as fact (for example "520% more calls" or "16% of ranking") and never say what Google's algorithm rewards. Say what Kabsi does.
- Never describe a feature marked **[COMING]** as available, and never give a date for it.

### 1.3 When to hand off to a person

Hand off at once for billing disputes and refunds, account access problems section 10 can't solve, legal or privacy requests, anything not in this knowledge base, angry customers (after one calm reply), and everything in section 13.

How to hand off: "I'll pass this to the Kabsi team. Please email hello@kabsi.co from the address on your account, and a person will reply." Where the app offers the "Need a hand?" box, point to it too.

### 1.4 Contact details

- Everyone, every country: **hello@kabsi.co**. A person replies.
- WhatsApp: **Kabsi has no WhatsApp number at the moment.** Never give one. For questions, sales and support people write to hello@kabsi.co, where a person answers. Kabsi never asks for a Google password or codes.

---

## 2. Product

### 2.1 Kabsi in one paragraph

Kabsi keeps a local business's Google Business Profile complete and current by following Google's own published guidance, and the owner approves every change. The owner invites the Kabsi group ID 5481006796 as a Manager on their Google Business Profile. Kabsi then shows a short list called **What needs your attention**, each item with a ready draft where Kabsi can write one. Every new Google review arrives by email with a reply already drafted in the reviewer's language, and the owner taps Review reply in the email, then Approve reply, Edit or Skip. Kabsi also drafts Google posts (one a week if the owner wants), checks photos before they go up, sets special hours for holidays, watches the listing for changes (Google Protection) and sends a factual report every Monday. Nothing is ever written to Google without the owner's explicit approval. Every business also gets a free review link and a QR code that open its Google review page. They work with the owner's own QR codes and NFC cards. Replies are one of five modules: Kabsi is not only a reply writer.

Main line: "Your reviews and listing. Taken care of." The line under it: "Kabsi looks after your business on Google: a reply ready for every new review, your hours and details kept right, and fresh posts. You just approve." Google's name never appears in Kabsi's own slogan, name or handles. The older line "Your Google Business Profile, taken care of." is retired.

Names in the app and on the website (K-02): Reviews, Google Profile, Google Protection, Get Reviews, Weekly Care Report, Settings. The app and the website no longer show a Profile Score, a Do now list or a points value, and the email button for a new review reads "Approve reply"; Edit, Skip and Open Kabsi sit under it as plain links. Every Kabsi email has exactly one yellow button. An owner who still says "Replies", "Profile Care", "Listing Shield", "Review Link and Card" or "Monday Report" means Reviews, Google Profile, Google Protection, Get Reviews and the Weekly Care Report.

### 2.1a The five modules

Kabsi is presented as five modules. Use these exact names.

- **Reviews:** every new review arrives by email with a reply drafted in the reviewer's language. The owner approves it with the button "Approve reply".
- **Google Profile:** one screen with a row for every detail Kabsi watches (business name, main category, phone, website, address, service area, opening hours, special hours, description, open status, attributes, verification): what Google shows, what you approved, a status (Matches what you approved, Differs on Google, Needs your OK, Not read yet) and when it was last checked. A detail you have not confirmed says "Not yet confirmed by you" and Kabsi never offers to put it back. At the top, "What needs attention": each change Google made with its two choices ("Google is right", "Keep my information"; before and after stacked on a phone) and what is missing or unconfirmed. A manager decides only what the owner allows and never a name, address, main category or open status change. Editors for the description, services and attributes come later. Posts, photo checks and special hours are all approved by the owner first. Home is where the owner starts: it says "You're all caught up" or "3 things need your attention", with the first items as cards.
- **Hours (inside Google Profile):** one screen for three things. **Opening hours**: the owner sets each day of the week as open or closed, with one to three periods a day, and closing after midnight is allowed. Review shows the week in plain words, and "Confirm and save to Google" is the approval of exactly that week; Kabsi sends it after a 10 second undo window and checks that Google shows it. From then on Google Protection treats those hours as the ones the owner approved, and the history says the owner changed them. **Special days**: a holiday, a late night or a closure for chosen dates, with the same confirmation. **Closed for a while**: the first day closed and the day the business opens again; Google has no reopening date, so Kabsi sets the days in between as closed special hours. A calendar shows the special days that are set. A manager can change hours only when the owner has let managers approve profile changes.
- **Google Protection:** compares the Google profile with the details the owner confirmed and alerts the owner when they differ. The email explains the difference ("Google shows Sunday closing at 18:00. You approved 22:00.") and links to the app, where the owner chooses "Google is right" or "Keep my information". A change waiting for the owner is a card on Home and at the top of the Google Profile screen, which also shows the status line "Google Protection: on, last check 09:14". Home's "What Kabsi did this week" shows each check.
- **Get Reviews:** a review link and QR code for everyone; they work with your own QR codes and NFC cards. The page shows "link activity", which is not the same as reviews: Google decides which reviews appear.
- **Weekly Care Report (live from 21 Oct 2026, P0.5-04):** an email every Monday at 08:00 local time, also kept under Insights. It starts with how many things Kabsi took care of that week, counted from the record of what Kabsi did (replies prepared, updates and photos published, changes to your profile found), then: the reviews (new, replies published, average rating), the Google Profile (checked how many times, changes found and how each was resolved, or "No important changes"), content (updates and photos published), customer activity for the week against the week before (views, calls, website clicks, direction requests; labelled as examples until Kabsi's Google connection is live), what needs you (nothing, or at most three lines), the Profile Coach's plan for the week (at most three lines), and the time saved. The time saved is an estimate and is never turned into money: 5 minutes for each reply published, 15 for each update (a post, a change to your hours or a profile detail), 10 for each batch of photos and 10 for each profile check that found something, with the working one tap away. On Pro it also shows how people found you. No review text and no customer names appear in it. Google's figures are kept with a report for 30 days and then removed from the report; Kabsi's own counts stay.

Plans are Free and Pro. Free is Get Reviews (the review link and QR code). Pro is all five modules.

### 2.1b What needs your attention

- Everything an owner can act on is one list of tasks, made by Kabsi's own checks (never typed in by hand): a reply ready for a new review, a review that needs more care, a reply Google did not show, a change Google Protection found, two different answers for one fact in About your business, a Google post or photos ready to approve, something that did not reach Google, Kabsi losing its Manager access, the plan ending within 7 days, and things missing from the profile (Business Knowledge, phone, website, main category, opening hours, the review link, photos, a recent post).
- Each task has a priority: **Urgent** (customer-facing information is wrong, a high-risk review, a reply Google refused, something that did not reach Google, lost access, the plan ending within 2 days), **Recommended** or **Nice to have**. There is no score and no points value. Each task has a short reason and opens the page where the owner does it. A task closes by itself when the thing is done (the reply is published, the question answered, the photos posted), usually within seconds.
- Home is the Action Center. It answers one question, "Do I need to do anything?". With nothing waiting it says **You're all caught up. Kabsi is taking care of the rest.** Otherwise it says how many things need the owner ("2 things need your attention") and shows at most 3 cards, urgent first and then oldest first; **See all** shows the rest. Each card says what happened, why it matters, what Kabsi suggests, the evidence (for a changed detail: "Google shows 18:00. You approved 22:00."), a risk label where there is one, what Kabsi prepared, one main button, **Later** (3 days), the time and a **History** link with what happened to that item. A high-risk review card says Kabsi did not draft a reply. The first time Kabsi reads your reviews, all the old unanswered ones are one card ("We found 23 unanswered reviews. Replies are ready.") with the list of low-risk replies to approve together and a link to read the rest one by one. Suggestions to make the profile more complete are listed lower on Home and never turn it from "all caught up" to "needs you". Home has no score, no chart and no quick-action tiles. Below the cards: **What Kabsi did this week** (read from Kabsi's activity record, routine checks as one line a day), one line on how many people opened the review link in the last 30 days ("That is activity, not reviews"), and a link to the Weekly Care Report.
- A strip under the business name always shows the Google connection, the last successful check and the plan. Green: "Google connected, Checked 14 minutes ago". If the last successful check is more than 6 hours old the strip turns amber and reads "Google check is late, Last checked 7 hours ago", so Home never looks healthy when checks are failing. If Kabsi lost access it is red. Businesses in early access (a person posts what you approve) show "Our team looks after your profile" with no check time, because Kabsi does not read their profile from Google yet. The plan part of the strip ("Free trial, 9 days left") is shown to the owner only; a manager does not see billing.
- Kabsi keeps to Google's limits: at most 5 changes a minute to one profile (Google allows 10). If Google stops answering, Kabsi pauses its Google calls for 5 minutes and then carries on; the checks that were due wait their turn, and nothing is sent twice.
- The owner (or a manager) can **do it**, put it off with **Later** (3 days) or **Skip** it (30 days); it comes back after that if it still applies. Nothing is sent to Google until the owner approves it. Never present the list as a ranking or as a promise of more customers or reviews.
- Nora, Kabsi's assistant in the dashboard, can read the same list (most important first) and say what the top one to three are in plain words, with a link to the page. She never mentions a score. She saves a fact into About your business only when the owner has just told her that fact.

### 2.1d Team, roles and who approves

- A business on Kabsi has three roles. **Owner**: sees everything, approves everything, manages the team, the plan and billing, and can disconnect Kabsi or delete the business. **Manager**: sees everything except billing and the plan, and approves only what the owner allows. **Staff**: adds photos and shares the review link; sees nothing else and approves nothing.
- The owner manages the team in **Settings, Team**: invite someone by email as a manager or staff member (they get an email and join when they sign in with that address; the invitation lasts 14 days), change a role, remove someone, or cancel an invitation. A business always keeps at least one owner. Every role change is recorded.
- **Who can approve**, per kind (review replies, Google posts, photos, hours, profile changes): by default only the owner. The owner can turn a kind on to let managers approve it too. Changes to the business name, address, main category or open status, and reviews that need more care, always need the owner, whatever the setting.
- Approval emails (Approve reply links) go to owners, plus any extra addresses the owner added in Settings, Emails. Managers approve in the app.
- **What Kabsi tells you, and when (Settings, "What Kabsi tells you"):** every email and every notice in the app goes through one notification engine. Owners and managers choose, for each kind of notice, when the email comes (the default, at once, in the daily email, or off) and whether it shows in the **bell** on Home (the bell lists what Kabsi told you, newest first, with Mark all as read; it approves nothing). The defaults: reviews that need extra care and urgent profile changes at once; a new review at once while the business is open (by the opening hours the owner confirmed; if there are none, it counts as open) and in the daily email after hours; everything else in the daily email, sent at the daily email time set in Settings. **Quiet hours** are 22:00 to 08:00 in the business's time zone: no emails are sent then, except an urgent change to the name, address, phone, main category, hours or open status on Google; a held email goes out at 08:00. The daily email groups the day's notices by kind, with the business name first ("Yawmiyati: 2 new reviews and 1 profile change"). These always stay on and cannot be switched off: urgent profile changes, Google access notices, billing and plan notices, account notices and replies from the team. Pausing emails for 7 days (Settings, Emails) stops the ones that can be switched off. The same event is never sent twice to the same address. Staff are told nothing about reviews or profile changes.
- **What every Kabsi email looks like:** one design for all of them: a sand background, one white card with the Kabsi mark, a heading, the content, one yellow button with black text, then a footer. The subject starts with the business name and then says what happened, for example "Yawmiyati: new 5-star review, reply ready" or "Yawmiyati: a review needs a little more care"; the line shown after the subject in the inbox repeats what matters. The footer says "Nothing is published until you approve it", "Why you got this" in one line, links to **Email settings** (and to **Unsubscribe from these emails** on every email you can switch off), how to reach the team (hello@kabsi.co), the seller (Hussein Slim, Dubai, United Arab Emirates) and that Kabsi is independent of Google. Every email also has a plain-text version. Emails you can switch off carry a one-click unsubscribe that Gmail and Apple Mail show as their own Unsubscribe button; it stops only that kind of notice, and you can turn it back on in Settings, Email settings. Kabsi never emails an address that bounced for good or marked an email as spam. Sign-in codes come from the sign-in system with the same look and carry no unsubscribe, because they cannot be switched off.
- An agency that looks after a client's profile is invited by the owner as Manager in Team, and approves only what the owner allows. There are no partner approval modes.
- Nora acts with the rights of the person signed in, never more.

### 2.1c Who can use Kabsi (eligibility)

Kabsi follows Google's Business Profile guidelines (support.google.com/business/answer/3038177), so it works only where Google does.

- **Works for:** a business that customers visit during stated hours (a shop, café, clinic, salon, garage or hotel); a service-area business that travels to customers (a plumber, cleaner or photographer) with a service area; a profile that is verified on Google and that the person owns or manages.
- **Not eligible:** online-only businesses with no in-person contact; rental or for-sale properties; PO boxes and virtual offices used as an address; other cases Google lists as not eligible.
- Kabsi cannot check verification itself, so setup asks. If the profile is not verified, the person verifies it on Google first (free, at business.google.com) and comes back. The terms let Kabsi pause the service for a profile that Google's guidelines do not allow.
- If Google's list changes, the site's `src/lib/eligibility.ts` changes first and this section follows.

### 2.1e Where things are in the app

On a computer the left menu has eight places: Home, Reviews, Get Reviews, Google Profile, Content (Posts and Photos), Insights (an overview and the Weekly Care Report), Business Knowledge and Settings. Google Profile has three tabs: Google Profile, Hours and Profile Coach. On a phone the bottom bar has five: Home, Reviews, Profile, Content and More; More opens Get Reviews, Insights, Business Knowledge and Settings, with help below. The plan is inside Settings, next to Notifications and Team, and the Weekly Care Report is inside Insights. The Insights overview says in one sentence how many customers interacted with your Google profile this month, compared with last month, with tiles for calls, website clicks, direction requests and times the profile was seen, daily charts under "See details" and, on Pro, how people found you (the search terms of the last full month). It says what changed and never why. Google's figures are read when you open the screen and are not stored. Until Kabsi's Google connection is live every figure is an example and is labelled Example. Every older address of an app page still opens the right screen. "Need a hand?" offers hello@kabsi.co (a person answers) and the guides. What a person sees follows their role: the owner sees everything; a manager sees everything except Plan and Team (billing and the team are the owner's); staff see only Photos and Get Reviews. A page that is not part of someone's role says so and offers Home.

### 2.2 [TIME-SENSITIVE] Current status: test mode and early access

- Kabsi's Google Business Profile API access is still under Google's review. Until approved, Kabsi runs in **test mode**: nothing is sent to Google automatically.
- Every app page shows a black banner: "Test mode: Kabsi isn't connected to Google yet. Nothing you post or save is sent to Google." Businesses in early access see an early-access note instead.
- **Early access:** a business can start before the approval. A person on the Kabsi team accepts your Google invitation and posts what you approve, within one working day. Drafting, the safety checks and your approval work as normal, and you still approve every word. Google Protection stays off until Kabsi connects to Google. Early access is limited to 20 businesses.
- Real businesses can sign up and finish setup now. A free trial or a paid plan starts when Google access works (section 4).
- The website and the app live at kabsi.co. Links sent earlier that use kabsi-app.lovable.app forward to the same page on kabsi.co.
- The assistant must not give a date for Google's approval. If asked: "We're waiting on Google's review and can't give a date. Your trial or plan starts when access works."

## 3. Setup and onboarding

### 3.1 Before you start

- A **verified** Google Business Profile on Google Maps that you **own or manage**, so you can add a Manager. Kabsi cannot check verification itself, so setup asks you. If "People and access" is missing, the listing may need to be verified or claimed first.
- A Google account or an email address you check (sign-in is with Google or an emailed code, no password).
- A few minutes.

### 3.2 Signing in

Signing up and logging in are the same steps. After the free check on /get-started, tap **Save your snapshot and continue**; the business you checked is kept, so setup starts with it already picked.

- **Continue with Google** (first choice): pick your Google account. Kabsi receives only your name and email address (openid, email and profile). It gives Kabsi no access to your Business Profile; that comes later through the Manager invitation.
- **Continue with email**: enter your email, pass the quick bot check, tap **Send me a code**, then type the 6-digit code from the email (there is no sign-in link). The code works for 10 minutes. Not there? Check spam, wait for the timer and tap **Send a new code**, or **Use a different email**.
- Limits that stop inbox flooding: at most 3 codes per email address in 15 minutes and 10 code requests per device or network in an hour. Throwaway email addresses (for example mailinator.com) cannot sign up. There are no passwords.

### 3.3 The setup steps (/start)

**Step 1: Find your business**

Search the name and city as on Google Maps (or name plus street or area), pick the result and tap **Yes, this is {business}**.

Then **One quick check**: "Kabsi works with a verified Google Business Profile that you own or manage. Is {business} yours on Google?"

- **Yes, I manage it and it's verified:** setup continues.
- **I'm not sure:** a 30-second check at business.google.com shows how to tell.
- **No, it isn't verified yet, or someone else manages it:** setup shows how to verify or ask for access on Google, and waits until then. Nothing is saved before you answer yes.

**Step 2: Give Kabsi access**

1. Tick the box: "I authorise Kabsi to manage review replies and profile updates for this business on Google, and to publish only what I approve."
2. Add the Kabsi group ID 5481006796 as a Manager. In the Google Maps app: tap your profile picture, then **Your business profiles**; choose the business, then **⋮** or **Profile settings**, then **People and access**; tap **Add**, paste the group ID 5481006796, choose **Manager**, then **Invite**. On a computer: open your Business Profile, then **More** (or **Menu**), **Business Profile settings**, **People and access**, **Add**, paste the group ID 5481006796, choose **Manager**, **Invite**. Invite the group, never the email address hello@kabsi.co.
3. The status box shows "Waiting for your invite…" and updates by itself, usually a few minutes after the invite once Kabsi is live on Google (see 2.2). Then it shows "Access received" and you get Kabsi's own access notice, "Kabsi is now a Manager of {business} on Google": what changed, what Kabsi can do, and how to remove Kabsi (Settings, **Disconnect Kabsi from Google**, or People and access). Kabsi sends this notice for every change it makes to its access to your profile, within 48 hours and separate from Google's own emails.
4. Tap **I've sent the invite, continue**, or **Do this later** and finish the other steps first.

A Manager can do everything Kabsi needs; only owners can add or remove people. You stay the owner and can remove Kabsi any time, without asking us: in Kabsi (Settings, **Disconnect Kabsi from Google**) or on Google (People and access).

**Step 3: About your business**

"Replies only use what you write here. If something isn't here, it's left out, never made up."

| Field | Required? | Why it matters |
|---|---|---|
| How you sign replies (for example "Luca, Trattoria Verde") | Required | Every reply ends with it |
| Tone: Warm, Formal, or Short & friendly | Choose one | Sets the voice of drafts |
| Business phone | Optional | Never written in a public reply. Unhappy customers are asked to contact you through the details on your Google profile, because Google can reject replies that contain phone numbers |
| Opening hours note (for example "Open daily 8am to midnight") | Optional | Used when a reviewer asks about hours |
| Anything you'd like mentioned (for example delivery area, parking) | Optional | Used only when a reviewer raises that topic |
| Staff names that may appear in replies (one at a time, up to 20, in Settings) | Optional | Lets replies thank the right person. Names not on the list are never used |
| Anything Kabsi should never say or promise (for example "Don't promise same-day delivery") | Optional | Drafts, posts and the safety check all follow it |
| Questions customers ask (up to 8 question and answer pairs) | Optional, in Settings only | Replies and posts can use these answers and nothing beyond them |

Tap **Save and continue**. Later changes in Settings, About your business apply to new drafts.

**Settings, About your business** (each fact on its own line, with its status):

- **Verified**: you gave it or confirmed it. Only Verified facts are used in replies and posts.
- **Needs your OK**: a fact Kabsi did not get from you (a suggestion, or something read from your website once that is possible). Replies and posts leave it out until you tap **Confirm**. **Not right** turns it down and Kabsi does not suggest that value again.
- **Out of date**: Kabsi asks you to check it again. Prices are asked again after 90 days, staff names after 180 days, opening hours notes after 60 days. Until you tap **Confirm**, replies and posts leave it out.
- **Edit** saves a new version (the earlier one is kept as history). **Delete** removes the fact and every earlier version for good, and Kabsi stops using it.
- When two sources give different answers about something customers see (hours, phone, services, prices), Kabsi asks "Kabsi found two different answers. Which is right?" and leaves that fact out of replies and posts until you choose. It never picks one for you.

Never-say examples: "Don't confirm the reviewer is a patient or mention any treatment." "Don't promise same-day delivery." "Don't mention the old location."

**Step 4: Your plan**

Owners start with the **14-day free trial** (no card; it begins when Google access works) and tap **Start trial**. Where no trial is offered, the step says card payments are coming and the owner taps **Finish setup**. The last screen, **You're set**, shows access and plan status; while a plan is still needed it says "Card payments in US dollars are coming. Until they open there is nothing to pay."

### 3.4 After setup

Statuses: Setup not finished, Waiting for Google access, Free, Active. A business goes active when Google access works and a free trial or paid plan is running. It is Free when access works and no trial or plan is running. Kabsi then drafts the backlog replies (10 on a trial, 20 on a paid plan), takes the Google Protection snapshot and starts the weekly cycle.

### 3.5 Recommended first actions

1. Home: read "things need your attention" and start with the first card.
2. Get reviews: copy your review link and print the QR code (three steps).
3. Posts: under **Write a post**, write a first post and save it.
4. Settings, About your business: add a few customer questions and never-say items.
5. Settings, Emails: choose your daily email time and time zone, and which notices reach you by email and in the bell.

## 4. Pricing and payment

### 4.1 Prices (US dollars, same in every country)

**[CHANGING]** This table is true today. Essentials ($19 a month or $190 a year) and Pro ($39 a month or $390 a year) will replace the plans below, and card checkout through Creem will be the only way to pay (see the 21 Oct block).

| Item | Price | Notes |
|---|---|---|
| Free | $0 | Review link, QR code, printable table card and a message to share. Never expires |
| Kabsi Pro, monthly | $19 a month | All five modules. Cancel any time |
| Kabsi Pro, yearly | $190 a year | Two months free |
| Extra location | $15 a month or $150 a year | One plan covers one Google profile; each extra profile is added on top |

- **Free trial: 14 days, no card**, for everyone. It starts when Kabsi's access to your Google profile works, so waiting for access costs you nothing. There is one trial per Google business.
- **Same everywhere:** Kabsi Pro is software only, at the same price in every country. Kabsi sells no cards. Every business everywhere gets a free review link and QR code, which work with your own QR codes and NFC cards (section 5).
- Pro includes everything in section 2: Reviews, Google Profile, Google Protection, Get Reviews and the Weekly Care Report.
- Monthly plans can be cancelled at any time. Yearly plans are refundable within 14 days.
- Kabsi may change prices for future purchases. A plan already paid for keeps its price.
- **[TIME-SENSITIVE]** The assistant may describe these prices once the pricing page shows them. If the pricing page still shows different prices, say so and hand off.

### 4.2 How to pay

By card, in US dollars, and nothing else. **[COMING]** Card checkout through Creem is not open yet. Until it opens there is nothing to pay: the Plan page says "Card payments in US dollars are coming. Until they open there is nothing to pay." Kabsi takes no crypto, cash or bank transfer, and no other payment app. Never give a wallet address or a payment ID. Anything else about paying: hand off.

### 4.3 When the trial and the plan start

- A **free trial** starts when Kabsi's access to your Google profile works and Google shows the profile as verified. It is 14 days. The Plan page shows the last day and how many days are left. It never starts for an early-access (concierge) business or a profile that is not verified.
- **One trial per business and per person:** one per Google listing (place) and one per Google account (the owner's Google sign-in or email; Gmail dots and +tags count as the same address). A business or account that already had a trial goes straight to a paid plan.
- **During the trial** you get the full product (new review drafts and publishing, Google Protection, the Weekly Care Report, one post a week, the review link and QR code, the assistant) with three limits: Kabsi lists every profile fix it finds but applies **3 of your choice** (the rest when you subscribe); it drafts replies for up to **10** older unanswered reviews (the rest when you subscribe); and after **100 drafts** it asks you to choose a plan or book a free setup call.
- A **paid plan** starts when payment is confirmed **and** Kabsi's access works. Time spent waiting for access doesn't count.
- If you pay during your trial, your paid plan starts the day the trial ends. You keep every trial day.
- If you pay before access works, the Plan page shows your plan as "Paid" and says: "Your plan starts the day Kabsi's access to your Google profile works, so you don't lose any days while you wait."
- **[TIME-SENSITIVE]** While Kabsi is in test mode (2.2), a trial or paid plan waits for Google access. In early access, it starts when the team has connected your business.

### 4.4 Renewals and reminders

Plans paid before 21 Oct 2026 don't renew by themselves; Kabsi never charges on its own. Home shows the plan and the days left in its top strip, and a card when the plan is about to end. **[COMING]** Renewing by card opens with card payments; until then the Plan page says card payments are coming.

During a trial, Kabsi sends a few short emails, each only once and only while it is true for your business: a welcome with the one next step (invite Kabsi as a Manager); if access is still missing, a reminder 1 hour, 24 hours and 72 hours after you asked for it (they stop as soon as Kabsi has access); a thank-you after your first approved reply; on day 2 what Kabsi has done so far; on day 7 your week, counted from the record of what Kabsi did and what you approved, with the yearly plan ($190 a year, two months free); on day 11 that your trial ends in 3 days, what happens next and both prices ($19 a month or $190 a year, plus tax where it applies); and on day 14 that the trial has ended (Kabsi keeps watching and drafting for 7 more days but publishes nothing until you choose a plan). These are the only trial emails: the older day 7, day 1 and last-day trial reminders were retired on 21 Oct 2026, so nobody gets two sets. There is no end-of-trial discount. The trial tips (day 2, day 7, day 11) can be switched off in Settings, Email settings; the welcome, access reminders and the day 14 notice cannot. If you do not continue, you may get one note about the replies and changes still waiting, about 17 days and 30 days after the trial ended, only if you said yes to marketing emails (in the UK, the EU and EEA, Saudi Arabia, the UAE and wherever your country is not known, always only with your yes). A business that pays and a business set up by the Kabsi team get none of the trial emails.

### 4.5 Refunds

- Yearly plans are refundable in full within 14 days of the plan starting. Email hello@kabsi.co. Kabsi refunds by the method you paid with where possible.
- A monthly plan runs to the end of the month paid for and is not refunded for that month. Cancelling a plan never removes Kabsi's Google access; disconnecting is a separate step the owner chooses (section 8.6).
- The unused part is refunded if a paid feature stops for good because Google changed its APIs, if Kabsi stops the service without you breaking the terms, or if the terms change in a way that matters and you don't agree.
- Nothing in the terms limits a refund you're entitled to by law.
- The assistant explains the policy but never approves or promises a specific refund. Hand off every refund request.

### 4.6 When a trial or plan ends

- **After a free trial (day 14 to day 21):** 7 days of grace. Kabsi keeps watching your profile and drafting replies, but publishes nothing; Home says what is waiting ("1 reply ready, 1 change caught"). Choose a plan and everything that is waiting can be approved. On day 21 without a plan, Kabsi removes its Manager access and emails you. **[TIME-SENSITIVE]** Until card payments are live, Kabsi does not remove access on day 21; the team gets in touch instead.
- **After a paid plan:** the business has no plan. Reply drafts, Google Protection and the Weekly Care Report stop. Kabsi's Google access is not removed by a plan ending; disconnecting is your choice (section 8.6).
- The review link and QR code keep working, for as long as Kabsi operates, and so does any NFC card that carries the link. Choose a plan on the Plan page to turn everything back on.

## 5. Review links and cards

A review link, QR code or NFC card opens the business's own Google review page. No rating screen, no filtering, no reward: every customer sees the same page. The public wording is: "Ask every customer the same way, as they visit. Never offer a reward."

### 5.1 Free for everyone: review links and QR codes

**Inside Kabsi (Get reviews, three steps)**

1. **Copy your review link.** Tap **Create my review link**: a short link (go.kabsi.co/{CODE}) and a QR code. Tap **Copy review link**.
2. **Print your QR code.** **Download QR** (SVG) or **Print** (a page saying "Leave us a Google review").
3. **Optional: use your own NFC card or tag.** If you own an NFC card, tag or sticker, write the same link on it with a free NFC writer app (section 5.4). Kabsi generates the link and the QR code; the tag is yours.
You can have up to 5 links per business (**Create another link**), for example one per spot, to compare opens. Each shows its opens for 7 days and can be switched off or on. Under each link, **When someone opens this link** lets you choose **Go straight to Google** (the default) or **Show the page** (the Google review button first, plus "Need help now? Message the manager" when you added a WhatsApp number in About your business). Everyone sees the same thing.

Share it in your own messages, Instagram bio, receipts, menus and follow-up emails.

**Without signing in: the free tool (/google-review-link)**

Search name and city to get Google's own review link, a PNG QR code and a printable counter card. Free, no sign-up, up to 20 searches per visitor per hour. Kabsi doesn't count opens of this Google link. Not found? Try the exact Maps name plus city. Kabsi limits how many business searches it runs a day, so Google's search costs stay small. If the limit is reached, the tool and the business search in setup say "Back soon" and work again the next day (UTC); nothing the owner has set up is affected.

**Without signing in: the free Google Profile Check (/google-profile-check)**

Search a business by name and city and see what customers see on Google, from public information only: rating, number of reviews, opening hours and whether it is open now, phone, website, category and whether the profile has photos. It does not use the owner's Google profile and changes nothing. Three to five findings are listed in plain words, each labelled **Urgent**, **Recommended** or **Nice to have**. There is no score, no ranking and no comparison with other businesses. Public information does not include review replies, the description, posts or photo dates, so the check says so and Kabsi looks at them only after the owner connects. The button is **Join early access** ("Kabsi can take care of these. You approve each one."). **Email me this check** sends the result to the address given; a box, unticked, says "Send me tips on managing my Google profile" and tips are sent only if it is ticked (Kabsi keeps the address, the business's Google Place ID, the choice, those words, the page and the time as proof). Free, no sign-up, 3 checks a day per visitor (the fourth is refused: "You have used your 3 free checks for today. Please come back tomorrow."), up to 10 requests a minute, and a bot check. Google's public details for a business are kept 24 hours, so a second check of the same business in a day does not ask Google again. When the daily limit on Google lookups is reached, or the check is paused, the page says **Back soon**. It also runs as the first two screens of setup (/get-started): "Which business is yours?" and "Here's what customers see", before any sign-up. Business details come from Google Maps. Kabsi is not partnered with Google.

### 5.2 Your own NFC cards and tags

Kabsi sells no NFC cards, anywhere. The review link and QR code work with your own QR codes and NFC cards: buy any blank NFC card or sticker online (chip type NTAG213 or NTAG215) and write your Kabsi review link onto it yourself (section 5.4), or simply print the QR code. Kabsi works 100% digitally.

**A Kabsi card you already have**

Kabsi cards that were sold before 21 Oct 2026 keep working. Kabsi issues no new ones.

- Tap a card that isn't linked ("This Kabsi card isn't set up yet"), sign in and link it; or in Get reviews, **Add a Kabsi card**, type the 6-character code under the QR, tap **Add**.
- Name cards ("Counter", "Table 4") with **Save name**. **Switch off** stops a card within about a minute; it then shows "This review link isn't active. Please ask the staff for help."

### 5.4 How to write your review link onto an NFC tag

You need: a blank NTAG213 or NTAG215 card or sticker, a phone that can write NFC, and a free NFC writer app such as NFC Tools.

1. In Kabsi, open Get reviews and tap **Create my review link** (or use an existing one). Tap **Copy review link**. It looks like https://go.kabsi.co/ABC234.
2. Use the link exactly as copied. Don't add "?s=q": that ending is for the printed QR code, so Kabsi can tell taps from scans.
3. Open NFC Tools and go to **Write**.
4. Tap **Add a record**, choose **URL / URI**, paste the link and confirm.
5. Tap **Write** and hold the phone against the tag until the app confirms.
6. Test it: tap the tag with another phone, ideally one iPhone and one Android. Your Google review page should open.
7. Optional: lock the tag in NFC Tools (the **Other** tab, **Lock tag**) so nobody can rewrite it. Locking is permanent. After locking, the tag can never be changed.

Good to know:

- Opens from your tag count under that review link and as taps in the weekly report. You can switch it off in Kabsi.
- Writing Google's own review link instead works, but Kabsi can't count opens or switch it off.
- **Add a Kabsi card** is for Kabsi card codes only, not tags you wrote yourself.
- NFC doesn't work through metal.

### 5.5 Where to put cards and QR codes

Where people pay or wait (counter, till, reception), on tables, on receipts, invoices, bags and menus (printed QR), and in follow-up messages. Trade-specific ideas are in section 7.

### 5.6 Rules for cards and links

- Ask every customer the same way. Never offer a discount, gift, prize or upgrade for a review; Google can remove those reviews. Cards say "Leave us a Google review", never "5 stars".
- Taps and scans are opens, not reviews. Kabsi never records who tapped.
- Deleting a business stops its review links and QR codes, and any NFC card that carries them.

## 7. Industry notes

Site examples are fictional and labelled. The same honesty rules apply to every trade. In every trade: ask every customer the same way, and never offer a discount, free item, gift or upgrade for a review.

### 7.1 Restaurants
Reviews land during service; drafts wait in email. Guests write in many languages; each draft matches. Illness and hygiene complaints get a calm draft with no quick Post button. Replies mention menu, delivery or reservations only if the owner gave those facts and the guest raised the topic; never invented dishes, prices, offers or discounts. Useful: special hours, dish photos checked, Google Protection for phone and hours. Card: on tables, at the host stand or till, printed QR on the bill folder or takeaway bag.

### 7.2 Cafés and bakeries
Post drafts after the morning rush. The weekly draft suits what's fresh (a seasonal pastry, a new blend). Early opening hours must be exact; set special hours for holidays. Arabic reviews get Arabic replies. Card: by the coffee machine or pastry counter, at the till, QR on cup sleeves or bread bags.

### 7.3 Clinics and dentists (patient privacy)
Drafts stay calm and general: no medical claims, no personal details, no admissions of fault, and they ask the reviewer to get in touch through the details on the profile. In many countries health privacy rules (HIPAA in the US, for example) mean a public reply shouldn't confirm someone is a patient or mention their care. Add "Don't confirm the reviewer is a patient or mention any treatment" under **Anything Kabsi should never say or promise**; drafts and the safety check follow it. Weekly drafts arrive on Tuesday. Card: at reception, QR on appointment cards or aftercare sheets, link in follow-up emails. This is not legal advice; privacy law questions go to a person.

### 7.4 Salons and barbers
Add team names so replies can thank the right stylist; names not on the list are never used. Photos of the work are checked; photos where a face is the main subject are flagged, so share the work, not the person. Card: at each station by the mirror, at reception, link in booking confirmations.

### 7.5 Hotels and B&Bs
Guests review in many languages; each draft matches. Check-in times, parking and breakfast hours come from About your business. Google Protection watches phone, address, website and hours; room photos are checked. Kabsi works with Google only, not booking sites. Card: at reception at check-out, in the room next to the Wi-Fi details, link in the thank-you email after the stay.

### 7.6 Garages and auto repair
Price disputes get a calm draft that asks the customer to get in touch through the details on the profile, with no quick Post button. Drafts never argue, admit fault or promise refunds or discounts. Google Protection matters for the phone number. Card: where customers pay and collect keys, QR on the invoice, link in the "your car is ready" message.

### 7.7 Shops and boutiques
Weekly drafts for new arrivals, with a Shop or Call button; never invented prices, offers or dates. Special hours for holiday openings. Each shop is its own business in Kabsi with its own plan. Card: at the till, QR on receipts or bags, link in order confirmations.

### 7.8 Florists
Drafts are warm for celebrations and gentle for sympathy orders, never adding details the customer didn't share. Special hours for busy seasons. Orders come by phone, so Google Protection watching the number matters. Arrangement photos checked. Card: tucked into each bouquet or delivery, at the counter, link in delivery confirmations.

---

## 8. Google policy and review best practice

### 8.1 How Google local results work

Google ranks local results by relevance, distance and prominence (support.google.com/business/answer/7091). Kabsi does the parts an owner controls: accurate details, a reply to every review, regular updates, and easy reviewing for every customer. It promises no rankings.

### 8.2 Replying to reviews (Google's steps)

1. Open your Business Profile (search your business name on Google while signed in, or go to business.google.com).
2. Select **Read reviews**.
3. Next to the review, select the **Reply** icon, write, and select **Reply**.

Google checks every reply against its content policies before it appears, usually within 10 minutes, sometimes longer. The reply shows under the review with the business name, and the customer is notified. You can edit or delete it later on Google.

A good reply: two to four sentences, in the customer's language, mentions one thing they said, no selling or discount codes, signed as the business, promises nothing you won't do.

### 8.3 Negative reviews

1. Wait until you're calm.
2. Thank them for telling you.
3. Name the problem in one sentence, without arguing in public.
4. Ask them to get in touch through the details on your profile. Don't write a phone number, email or link in the reply: Google can reject replies that contain them.
5. Keep it short and sign as the business.

Never: argue about who is right, share the customer's details, accuse them of lying, or offer discounts or refunds for changing or removing the review (Google treats that as fake engagement). Replying promptly is Google's advice.

### 8.4 Removing reviews

- Nobody outside Google can remove a review, whatever they charge. Google removes reviews that break its policies (spam and fake engagement, profanity, harassment or hate speech, off-topic content, personal information), not reviews that are simply negative.
- **Report from your profile:** open your Business Profile, **Read reviews**, select the **Report** icon next to the review, choose the reason, **Send report**.
- **Or use Google's Reviews Management Tool:** sign in with the account that manages the profile, choose the business, **Continue**, **Report a new review for removal**, choose the reason, **Submit**. A decision usually takes several days. Statuses: "Decision pending", "Report reviewed - no policy violation", "Escalated - check your email for updates". If the review stays up, you can appeal once from the same tool.
- While you wait, reply calmly. Help page: support.google.com/business/answer/4596773.

### 8.5 Asking for reviews

- Get your link from your profile (**Read reviews**, then **Get more reviews**, then **Copy**; the QR code is available on a computer browser), or use Kabsi's free tool.
- Ask everyone the same way. Google prohibits offering incentives (free or discounted goods or services) for reviews, and asking only customers you expect to be happy.
- An honest mix of reviews is more convincing to readers anyway.

### 8.6 Manager vs Owner

| | Owner | Manager |
|---|---|---|
| Edit business information | Yes | Yes |
| Reply to reviews | Yes | Yes |
| Add posts and photos | Yes | Yes |
| Add or remove people | Yes | No |
| Remove the profile | Yes | No |

- Never share your Google password; add people as Managers. Kabsi is a Manager, and you stay the owner.
- New owners and managers wait 7 days before they can use some features, such as removing other users (Google's rule).
- **To remove Kabsi:** on your Business Profile open **Menu** (or **More**), then **Business Profile settings**, then **People and access**, select Kabsi Clients (group ID 5481006796) and choose **Remove person**. Only owners can remove users. Kabsi stops reading and posting at once.

### 8.7 Google content rules Kabsi follows

Kabsi keeps Google content for at most 30 days, as Google's policy requires (details in 9.7; one retention table sets every limit and the daily retention job reads it), and follows the Google API Services User Data Policy, including the Limited Use requirements. Google Protection is covered in the FAQ (section 11); Google Q&A is covered in 2.14.
